title: Better Posture Linked to Better Decision Making and Mood
author: Jake Currie

But don’t worry, you’re not alone. Studies have shown that the vast majority of people who use digital devices (like the one you’re using to read this) have less-than-ideal posture that can result in musculoskeletal pain. According to a new study published in the British Journal of Psychology, poor posture can affect your decision making, too.Like all good psychological experiments, this one involved a bit of trickery, but for good reasons. Previous studies have shown more “expansive” posture can influence behavior and moods, but many of these involved experimenters prompting the participants to adopt the postures, which means they could be responding to the prompts, rather than the postures.
